title: Operational Incident Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of operational incident handling in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to diagnosing a failed deployment.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers operational incident handling within observability and operations. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use operational incident handling to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Operational Incident Handling matters because it is part of observability and operations. In practice, focus on a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Diagnosing a failed deployment
items.text: For diagnosing a failed deployment, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

items.title: Investigating elevated error rates
items.text: Use investigating elevated error rates to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

items.title: Identifying resource exhaustion
items.text: Use identifying resource exhaustion as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Reviewing logs and traces
items.text: For reviewing logs and traces, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

items.title: Incident documentation and prevention
items.text: Use incident documentation and prevention as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Operational Incident Handling
content_blocks.run_instructions: Try one existing-style ID and the documented missing-resource case.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Diagnosing a failed deployment”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Operational Incident Handling”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Diagnosing a failed deployment” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Operational Incident Handling, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Operational Incident Handling belongs to the broader goal of a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
